name: Pohlman, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Condemarin's holding is limited and does not control the constitutionality of the 2017 GIA's damages cap because the statutes are different and Condemarin lacked a majority rationale.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Recused, did not participate in the decision.

name: Associate Chief Justice Pearce
description: Recused, did not participate in the decision.

name: ASSOCIATE CHIEF JUSTICE PEARCE
description: Concurred, arguing that the court clarified the Brickey standard to prevent prosecutorial bad faith or harassment while allowing the State to refile charges under specific conditions, and that the Victims' Rights Amendment abrogated the discovery purpose of preliminary hearings.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE DURRANT
description: Concurred, argued that subsections (2)(b) and the waiver component of (2)(c) of the Plea Withdrawal Statute are unconstitutional as they violate the separation of powers by being procedural rules enacted by the legislature.

name: ASSOCIATE CHIEF JUSTICE PEARCE
description: Recused himself and did not participate.

name: JUSTICE HAGEN
description: Concurred, argued that the Legislature failed to follow constitutional requirements for submitting and publishing Amendment D, rendering it void.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Concurred, argued that Baugh's counsel was objectively unreasonable for failing to request specific unanimity instructions, leading to a significant risk of a non-unanimous verdict and prejudice.

name: DURRANT, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the property tax exemption applies only when a nonprofit entity uses its property exclusively for charitable purposes, and Sports Medicine did not meet this standard because its market-rate testing and vacant space were not exclusively charitable uses.

name: JUSTICE POHLMAN
description: Concurred, argued that Bingham failed to demonstrate that the Utah Health Care Malpractice Act's four-year statute of repose is unconstitutional under the Open Courts Clause, Uniform Operation of Laws Provision, or the Equal Protection Clause, as the statute addresses a clear social or economic evil (healthcare crisis) through non-arbitrary and reasonable means.

name: Justice Hagen
description: Concurred, authored the opinion affirming the Commission's decision, finding that the County failed to show the Aircraft Valuation Law was unconstitutional as applied or on its face.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court, finding that Kell failed to demonstrate how the dismissal of his claim, after a five-year delay, violated his constitutional rights.

name: Associate Chief Justice Pearce
description: Concurred, argued that the Utah Constitution's Bail Provision does not forbid judges from setting bail for defendants not guaranteed bail, but rather allows judicial discretion.

name: The Court
description: Concurred, holding that petitioners failed to demonstrate that a school district's tax increase is subject to a referendum under the Utah Constitution or relevant statutes.

name: Justice Himonas
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion holding that improper communications by authoritative court personnel triggered a rebuttable presumption of prejudice, requiring the State to prove harmlessness beyond a reasonable doubt.

name: Justice Petersen
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's balancing test for prejudice was unnecessary and that the district court's original handling of the matter was sufficient.

name: Lee, Associate Chief Justice
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court, affirming the dismissal of zoning challenges and declining to rule on tax provisions due to mootness.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion, concluding Laws lacked standing due to insufficient particularized injury and affirming the denial of attorney fees to Grayeyes.

name: Associate Chief Justice Lee
description: Concurred, argued that Laws lacked standing and Grayeyes was not entitled to attorney fees under the private attorney general doctrine, elaborating on the basis for dismissal on standing grounds and identifying an alternative ground for denying attorney fees.

name: Justice Pearce
description: Concurred, argued that the Utah Constitution might not prevent the Legislature from granting standing to a plaintiff who cannot meet traditional standing requirements, questioning the reliance on federal and secondary sources in standing jurisprudence.

name: Justice Pearce
description: Concurred, argued that most of Patterson's claims were time-barred under the PCRA, but two claims based on newly discovered evidence should be remanded.

name: Associate Chief Justice Lee
description: Concurred, argued that Patterson's claims were time-barred and no egregious injustice exception applied, but parts of the majority's constitutional analysis were premature and unnecessary.

name: Justice Himonas
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion, arguing that Utah courts have common-law authority to adjudicate sex-change petitions, which are analogous to name-change petitions, and established a two-prong test for approval.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Concurred in the judgment but dissented in part, arguing the standard for sex changes should be derived from statutory interpretation of "proper cause" for name changes, applied uniformly, rather than relying on broad common-law authority.

name: Associate Chief Justice Lee
description: Dissented, arguing the court lacked jurisdiction for non-adversarial matters and overstepped its judicial power by creating new law for "gender identity" instead of interpreting the statute's original meaning of "biological sex."

name: Justice Himonas
description: Concurred, arguing that the district court erred in dismissing the case because the plaintiffs sufficiently alleged that the death was not caused by an inherent risk, despite the Act being applicable and constitutional.
